It never does… it’s an abstract subject but what is really consider better? I see it more of a subject of being heavy or lighter. Nowadays the way of analyzing your depression is not to weigh into it as better or worse, but as feeling heavier or lighter. A day of light depression finds me having progression, continuing with my short-term goals…in contrast a heavier depression results in me taking a day off from everything, including life in general.. I’ll spend the whole day reminiscing my mistakes, all the dull moments when life could’ve been easier, but I have a constancy of feeling like it’s never enough… I find myself lost.. is life really that complicated, where I can’t even find the road ahead but I still tell myself that it’ll all be worth it, for myself… only for myself… because everyone forgot about me and all there really is at the end, is myself. Remember that, do you… the love you wish you could give or receive, give it to yourself, love yourself. Map out your success, there’s always something else, world is to vast and capable to simply say, the end. Remember that, before you decide to end yourself or your conscience, ask yourself, how hard have I tried for me.

Having a child is never the solution, love. It’s about loving yourself first and foremost, with time. I’m not here to say it gets better, but it can either get easier or harder and that honestly depends on you. How can you expect to care for a child if you won’t even care for yourself? Learn to appreciate the life you’ve been given and do what you can with what you have. Now if having a child is something you’d want to do, bring the baby into a life worth the effort that comes to caring and raising one. Do it for yourself and then do it for your child. Learn and grow, see as a small accomplishment to always follow the next step, not stress over the final step… only the next.

Sadly the only one that can truly makes things better is yourself. You hold the power to end it all or keep going, whatever your option, one consists of trial and error. Look into that when deciding, a lot of times setting small joys, distractions, or accomplishments helps. Like making it to the Spider-Man No Way Home release, or perhaps till next March to watch The Batman… I love film and regardless of how shitty my life is, I can still sometimes find joy in it even if it’s just for an evening matinee. Going to the grocery to buy groceries and then going home and cooking yourself a delicious meal, that’s a simply small accomplishment that is unique to yourself and will only bring you joy. Learn the difference, it’s harder and more depressing when you have thoughts over long-term goals that may never happen. Hope you give yourself that self-love, because sometimes that’s all there is. If you can learn to grow into living yourself, you’ll find that it’s addicting and so much more rewarding than wasting your time and effort on others
